properties.description: 15 tests in four files, each written before the code it pins. crates/reflow2-core/tests/built_work_reads_as_built.rs (5): a Component whose allocated capabilities are all realized or verified reads `built` and its stored status is unchanged; one with no built evidence (planned or in-progress capabilities, a planned file, a failing check) reads `not_built`; one with some function unbuilt, or a file while a hosted capability is unbuilt, reads `partly_built`, and a part with only a passing check of its own reads `built`; a capability an accepted Decision withdrew is not counted; and understated_status names exactly the planned components whose reading is not `not_built`. crates/reflow2-core/tests/awaiting_the_owners_word.rs (4): a delivered proposed requirement is listed with the capability that delivers it and the call that closes it; a proposed idea whose promotion landed is listed with what it became, and the listed ideas are exactly the ones decision_overtaken_by_promotion reports; an accepted requirement, an accepted idea, an undelivered requirement and an idea whose target has not landed are not listed; loop_status lists them for a named contributor, says so in `next`, keeps `clean`, leaves the unscoped list empty, and moves no status. crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/built_work_reads_as_built_on_the_wire.rs (3): get_node and scan_nodes (brief and full) carry `built_reading` on every Component and on no other type, beside an untouched status, with every key they carried before; loop_status carries `awaiting_word` scoped and `[]` unscoped. crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_scoped_loop_status_fits_its_budget.rs (3), added 2026-10-14 after review: the scoped loop_status with many awaiting items fits the 30,000-character default and keeps every id, closing call and count; an explicit budget_chars is honoured, with withheld rows named; and scan_nodes fits the budget whole-reply and honours a smaller one. The ship-step instruction is pinned separately by tools/skill_lint.py's ship-step contract, and the reply sizes by tools/replies_are_bounded.py.
properties.findings: 2026-10-14, after review. Review found the scoped loop_status over the 30,000-character reply budget flo2.io's gateway holds replies to. tests/a_scoped_loop_status_fits_its_budget.rs (3 tests) was written first, at 433b5ce9b, and FAILED 3 of 3 at 4fbee0ed5: the scoped reply with 80 delivered requirements was 71,877 characters, budget_chars was refused as not a parameter, and scan_nodes over 120 requirements answered 39,937. replies_are_bounded.py, extended to the argument-taking reads, FAILED on 10 cases. With the bound (8f7551459): 3 of 3 pass, the reply_budget unit tests pass (11), replies_are_bounded is OK (scoped loop_status 29,065, every scan under 30,000), and the earlier 12 tests, the touched loop_status and scan_nodes tests and tools.rs pass. Clippy, fmt, skill lint and 14 binary-driven gates are clean. One lib test, registry_http an_idle_design_is_closed_and_one_serving_a_request_is_not, failed once in a parallel run and passed 3 of 3 alone; it is untouched here, and its cause was not established. Measured on main's design copy, compact: scoped loop_status went from 10,249 on main and 38,939 unbounded to 27,885, keeping all 51 rows with names and evidence cut. With budget_chars 15,000 it is 14,658, with 8 of 51 rows shown. Unscoped it is 10,356. Full scans of large types are 25,939 to 27,940, against 37,645 to 40,110 on main. Earlier run, 2026-10-13: 12 of 12 passed after failing first; the core suite passed (2097); the workspace passed 3303 with one test expectation moved; built_reading read 61 built, 28 partly built and 20 not built of 109 components; awaiting_word held 51 (38 requirements and 13 ideas).
